name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz mine strikes 26 Nov; Red Sea attacks
summary: Iran's Guards say two tankers hit Hormuz mines on 26 Nov; crossings fell over 40% on 17–23 Nov; Red Sea ports hit
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines north of Khasab on 26 Nov while crossing Hormuz by an unauthorised route, and said the force is keeping the strait closed (Deccan Herald, Reuters wire). UKMTO reported a projectile blast near a tanker west of Dubai on 26 Nov (Times of Israel). Crossings fell to 125 ships on 17–23 Nov from 226 on 1–7 Nov, and the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Red Sea ports on 25 Nov, so two chokepoints remain disrupted.
for_you: Expect longer shipping times and higher freight and insurance costs on goods routed via the Gulf and Red Sea.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded and Red Sea disrupted = Alert

sources.title: Deccan Herald — Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab
Times of Israel — Projectile said to cause explosion near tanker west of Dubai

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
